title: Consistency
summary: A theory is consistent when its rules do not derive an explicit contradiction.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared formal proof systems context is fixed.

content.plain: A theory is consistent when its rules do not derive an explicit contradiction.
content.exact: A theory T is syntactically consistent when no formula P has both T⊢P and T⊢¬P; equivalent formulations require assumptions about the logic.
content.example: A model of a sound classical theory witnesses consistency relative to the surrounding metatheory.
content.caveat: Consistency is always relative to a formalization and often established only relative to a stronger background system.
